name: AOL Australia
summary: America Online's Australian service: launched 1998 from a 50/50 AOL-Bertelsmann JV (announced Oct 1997); restructured as a 50/50 AOL-AAPT joint venture (announced 30 Mar 2000) with exclusive AOL/CompuServe rights across PC and wireless platforms; became the three-way AOL|7 venture with Seven Network (merging Seven's i7 portal, Oct 2001); sold to Primus Telecommunications Feb 2004, which ran the AOL-branded ISP under licence until AOL access was withdrawn 31 May 2010.

events.details: AOL Australia JV announced 7 Oct 1997 (with Bertelsmann); service launched 1998 (beta from late April 1998; earliest aol.net.au capture 25 Apr 1998).

America Online and AAPT announced a new 50/50 joint venture to operate AOL Australia, with AOL taking over Bertelsmann's 50% interest (subject to FIRB approval). The JV held exclusive rights to offer the AOL and CompuServe services on PC and mobile wireless platforms in Australia, planned an integrated wireless-content portal over AAPT's CDMA network, and gave AOL Australia access to AAPT's 650,000-strong retail base and network infrastructure; MD Carol Veriga stepped down (Dr Brett Wayn appointed GM).

refs.label: ASX announcement (AAPT Limited, 30 Mar 2000): 'AAPT & America Online ann. New AOL Australia JV'

events.details: Three-way AOL|7 joint venture formed by America Online, Seven Network and AAPT (equal thirds), merging Seven's i7 online service (launched Sep 2000) with the AOL site to deliver broadband content and cross-promotion between Seven, Pacific Publications and the ISP.

refs.label: Wikipedia: Yahoo! Australia / i7 - Seven founded i7 Sep 2000, partnered with AOL Oct 2001 to establish the AOL7 joint venture

events.details: AOL, Seven and AAPT sold the AOL|7 joint venture to Primus Telecommunications for just over $23 million (Seven receiving more than $23m cash including its i7 investment; AAPT $7.5m for its one-third stake). Primus gained an exclusive licence to operate the AOL-branded internet service in Australia with no member disruption; AAPT took sole management of its ~48,000 smartchat dial-up/broadband customers back in-house.

refs.label: SMH (11 Feb 2004): 'AOL, Seven, AAPT sell joint venture'
iTnews (10 Feb 2004): 'Primus snaps up AOL|7' - acquired for just over $23m

events.details: Primus withdrew AOL dialup/broadband access in Australia 31 May 2010, ending the AOL-branded service.

The ABR entity AOL AUSTRALIA PTY LTD (ACN 633 469 468, SA) was registered only 16 May 2019 and is unrelated to the historical 1998-2010 AOL Australia / AOL|7 service; the earlier JV ran through AAPT/Seven and then under Primus Telecommunications' licence, not this company.
